T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — BOJ September/December rate hike expectations, near-term yen pressure
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — BOJ hike path into 2027, JGB yield spillovers to UST, Japan fiscal trajectory under Takaichi

**Synopsis:**
US Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly pressured Japan to accelerate BOJ rate hikes and curtail expansionary fiscal policy (Abenomics-style stimulus), framing the July joint yen intervention as leverage. The BOJ is now effectively locked into a September hike, with Oxford Economics projecting additional hikes in December 2026 and April 2027. Japan's record budget requests and JGB yields at 30-year highs are flagged as a spillover risk to US Treasury yields. Bessent's remarks signal Washington's concern that a weak yen and loose Japanese fiscal policy could destabilize global fixed income markets, with direct implications for US rates.
